title: Claim-Carrying Vulnerability Report (CCVR) v0.1
description: A machine-checkable claim attached to a vulnerability report. The checker (CRDS) returns REFUTED with an unsat-core certificate, CONFIRMED if a witness reproduces, or ESCALATE. Prose stays for humans; the claim is what the machine triages. Carrying the claim is what makes sound automatic triage possible: the checker binds to the exact function, decision point, and field-level predicate instead of mining them from prose.

version.description: release or commit the claim is made against

build_config.description: feature flags that must hold for the path to exist

decision_point.description: the branch / match-success / sink the claim is about

predicate.description: the field-level condition asserted to hold at the decision point under the bug outcome
examples: creds inequality is reachable at match-success (credential compare skipped when conn->creds==NULL)
length into fixed buffer can exceed its capacity at the sink
connections differing in field X are matched

dimension_fields.description: the exact record fields the claim concerns (not a coarse dimension word)

branch_outcome.description: which way the decision goes for the bug to manifest

witness.description: optional reproduction the checker can run in a sandbox (verdict only). If present and it reproduces on target and not on the fixed build, the report is CONFIRMED.

x-checker-outcomes.REFUTED: PC(decision_point, branch_outcome) AND predicate is UNSAT; the returned unsat core is the set of guards in the maintainer's own code that make the claim impossible. A grounded-slop report that carries a precise but false claim lands here, with a proof.
x-checker-outcomes.ESCALATE: cannot refute and no witness: the claim names an unenforced path (as in a genuine bug) or lies outside the decidable fragment. Human time is spent only here.
x-checker-outcomes.CONFIRMED: a carried witness reproduces on the target and not on the fixed build.

claim.predicate: creds inequality reaches match-success when conn->creds==NULL

x-worked-example-CVE-2026-19931.checker_result: ESCALATE: forced_fields(url_match_auth) = {} on 8.21.0, so the credential equality is NOT forced on the match path; the checker correctly does not refute, and the genuine report is preserved. The prose-mined dimension route wrongly REFUTED it because credentials are forced by other gates (proxy_info_matches), on other paths. Carrying the function-and-field-precise claim restores soundness.
